<details><summary>AI review</summary>

`workers/modules/dedicated-worker-import-failure.html` currently only checks top-level 1-argument `importScripts('empty-worker.js')` in `Window` -> `new Worker(url, { type: 'module' })` (and awaits `onmessage` without rejecting on `onerror`, stalling until timeout on uncaught errors). Would it make sense to expand it in a companion WPT PR to cover the remaining cases of `worker global scope`'s `type`?
- Zero-argument `importScripts()` and invalid-URL `importScripts('http://invalid:123$')` in a `{ type: 'module' }` dedicated worker, where `import scripts into worker global scope` step 1 throws `TypeError` before step 3's empty-list return and step 5's URL parsing. For example, `new Worker(blobURLWithZeroArgImportScripts, { type: 'module' })` throws `TypeError` in Chrome Canary 160, whereas Firefox Nightly 160 returns `undefined` without throwing because [`workerinternals::Load`](https://github.com/mozilla-firefox/firefox/blob/d7161e35da7704cff60e48ee86fb7747ffcc93c7/dom/workers/ScriptLoader.cpp#L1944-L1946) returns early on empty `aScriptURLs` before [`WorkerScriptLoader::CreateScriptRequests`](https://github.com/mozilla-firefox/firefox/blob/d7161e35da7704cff60e48ee86fb7747ffcc93c7/dom/workers/ScriptLoader.cpp#L555-L563) checks `WorkerType::Module`.
- Distinguishing `worker global scope`'s `type` from the active script's type, plus explicit `{ type: 'classic' }`: `new Worker('resources/import-scripts-worker.js', { type: 'classic' })`, a `{ type: 'classic' }` dedicated worker dynamically `import()`ing a module that calls `importScripts()`, and a `{ type: 'module' }` dedicated worker running `setTimeout("importScripts(...)", 0)`.
- Nested dedicated workers (`new Worker(url, { type: 'module' })` from a classic dedicated worker and `new Worker(url, { type: 'classic' })` from a module dedicated worker).

</details>
